name: weekly-sales-report

summary.goal: Every Monday morning, turn last week's sales export into a short Excel summary and leave an email draft with it for your manager, so the report is ready to check and send.
summary.used_by: You, and your manager as the reader of the email
summary.starts: On its own every Monday at 8:00, or when you ask for it
summary.from_where: The weekly sales export in your OneDrive folder Sales/Exports
summary.to_where: An Excel file in Sales/Reports and an email draft in your Gmail
summary.from_what: One CSV file of last week's orders
summary.to_what: A one-page Excel summary: totals per product and per region, and the five largest orders

reuse.recommendation: Build new, using invoice-summary as a model. It already reads this kind of CSV export, but it summarizes invoices, not orders, and it cannot run on a schedule or write an email.

candidates.name: invoice-summary
candidates.does: Turns a monthly invoice CSV export into an Excel summary with totals and a chart.
candidates.lacks: Order fields (product, region), a weekly period, the email draft, and a schedule.
candidates.takes: Adapting a copy: new columns, a weekly period, and an email step.

candidates.name: xlsx
candidates.lacks: Everything specific to the sales report; it is a general file tool.
candidates.takes: Nothing: the new procedure uses it for the Excel step.

steps.goal: Use the newest CSV in Sales/Exports, and stop with a clear message if there is none from last week.
Make sure the columns and dates are what the report expects, so a changed export is noticed instead of giving wrong totals.
Totals per product and per region, and the five largest orders, in one Excel sheet.
Keep every week's report in Sales/Reports, named by the week it covers.
A short note with the three main numbers and the file attached, left as a draft for you to check and send.

will: Read the newest export in Sales/Exports
Create one new Excel file each week in Sales/Reports
Create one email draft in your Gmail
wont: Send any email: you send the draft yourself
Change or delete the export files

actions.action: Reads the sales export in Sales/Exports
Saves the Excel summary in Sales/Reports
actions.note: A new file each week; an existing file is never replaced.

actions.action: Creates the email to your manager in Gmail
actions.note: You check it and press send.

access: Your OneDrive folders Sales/Exports (read) and Sales/Reports (write)

assumed.why: You wrote to me in English.
The export's amounts are in EUR.

assumed.value: Plain, with one bar chart of totals per region

questions.question: Should the report go to your manager as an email draft, or only be saved as a file?
questions.recommended: An email draft that you send yourself.

questions.question: What is your manager's email address?
questions.recommended: No default: I need the address to fill in the draft.
questions.why: It is not in your files or earlier messages.

questions.question: If there is no export from last week on Monday morning, what should happen?
questions.recommended: Skip that week and leave a short note in Sales/Reports saying the export was missing.
questions.why: Nothing is sent or guessed, and you see why the report is missing.

questions.question: Is 8:00 on Monday a good time for it to run?
questions.why: Your exports arrive on Sunday evening.

details.route: Main route (not a hook or a mod, so nothing is handed off).
types: Scheduled and recurring: an unattended run only prepares the draft and the file, never sends.
Documents and files: OneDrive folders may be read-only while syncing; failures are reported, not skipped.
Data: the column check runs before any total is computed.
details.placement: Personal skills folder `~/.claude/skills/weekly-sales-report`, because it uses your own OneDrive and Gmail rather than one project's files.
details.effort: A bundled Python script does the totals; the main agent writes the email text at normal effort.
details.design: Internal output (Excel and email), so no page design is needed and no design review applies.

files.purpose: The procedure, its checks, and what it cannot do.
Reads the CSV, checks the columns, and writes the Excel summary.
Saved test cases: a normal week, a missing export, and a changed column.

lessons.note: Unattended runs prepare drafts only; sending stays with you.
OneDrive read-only folders are reported, not skipped silently.

installs.name: openpyxl
installs.why: Writes the Excel file from the script.

notes: The schedule is set up with the `schedule` skill after the build is approved and tested.
